wiki_waves_speed_some_capped: Most enemies do not speed up at all as the waves go on. A few — bosses mainly — gain up to {0} per wave until wave {1}. Their movement speed does not increase after that, so slows retain their late-run value.

trait_entropy_engine_desc: Every second, all enemies lose a portion of their CURRENT health. Cannot kill - it only softens tanks so your turrets can finish them.
trait_frozen_fragility_desc: Frozen enemies take much more damage, creating burst windows for sniper and laser builds.
trait_lucky_charm_desc: Spec card offers and rerolls skew toward higher grades.

trait_reinforced_ammo_desc: Improves base damage for all projectile and beam attacks.

trait_singularity_core_desc: Converts lifetime spending into permanent in-run damage scaling, ideal for endless play.
trait_thermal_cascade_desc: Burning enemies can spread flames to nearby enemies, creating chain DoT clears.

turret_basic_turret_desc: A reliable single-target turret with balanced damage, range, and fire rate. Simple, cheap, and effective through upgrades.
turret_basic_turret_path_a_desc: Fires two weaker shots per attack, increasing hit frequency and making it excellent against fast enemies and on-hit effects.
turret_basic_turret_path_b_desc: A long-range heavy cannon that fires slow but devastating shots. Best used against bosses, elites, and high-health enemies.
turret_basic_turret_tier2_desc: Armor Break lingers longer and now gnaws at the target's current HP.
turret_frost_turret_desc: Fires chilling shots that slow enemies. A strong control turret that gives your damage towers more time to attack.
turret_void_turret_desc: Corrodes enemy defenses, making them more vulnerable to all damage.
turret_toxin_turret_desc: Every hit deals bonus pure damage that ignores enemy defenses entirely.
turret_railgun_turret_desc: Slow but devastating single hits that leave the target exposed to more damage from everything else.
turret_frost_turret_path_a_desc: Adds short freeze bursts to its attacks, briefly stopping enemies in place. Great for interrupting dangerous enemies and creating burst windows.
turret_frost_turret_path_b_desc: Spreads slow effects around the target, controlling groups instead of single enemies. Excellent against dense waves.
turret_frost_turret_tier2_desc: Slow strength is greatly reinforced, regardless of evolution path.
turret_inferno_turret_desc: Applies burning damage over time. Burns stack with every hit, so attack speed and burn bonuses multiply total burn damage.
turret_inferno_turret_path_a_desc: Fires burning projectiles that explode on impact, damaging enemies around the target.
turret_inferno_turret_path_b_desc: Repeated hits stack additional burn damage on the same enemy. Excellent for long fights and endless scaling.
turret_inferno_turret_tier2_desc: Burn intensity is greatly reinforced, regardless of evolution path.
turret_laser_turret_desc: Locks onto one enemy with a continuous beam. Damage ramps up the longer the beam holds the same target, so it excels against tanks that stay in range.
turret_laser_turret_path_a_desc: Splits its beam across multiple enemies. Trades single-target power for reliable crowd pressure.
turret_laser_turret_path_b_desc: Focuses on one target and ramps up beam damage the longer it holds contact. At full ramp it also executes a portion of the target's missing health every second. A dedicated boss and tank killer.
turret_laser_turret_tier2_desc: Sustained fire deals extra damage based on the target's remaining HP, regardless of evolution path.
turret_lightning_turret_desc: Fires charged shots that chain between nearby enemies. A flexible anti-swarm turret with strong wave-clear potential.
turret_lightning_turret_path_a_desc: Extends lightning chains to more enemies, spreading damage across large groups. Best against packed waves.
turret_lightning_turret_path_b_desc: Adds percentage-based damage to chained enemies, helping it stay useful against tanks and high-health targets.
turret_lightning_turret_tier2_desc: Hits deal extra damage based on the target's remaining HP, regardless of evolution path.
turret_radar_turret_desc: Reveals stealth enemies in a wide area. Upgrades extend its reveal range. Essential against hidden threats, but has no direct damage
turret_radar_turret_path_a_desc: Marks every enemy in range, not only stealth ones. Marked enemies take increased damage from all sources. Best on a choke point, where it amplifies your whole kill zone.
turret_radar_turret_path_b_desc: Nearby turrets gain extra range and can target stealth enemies anywhere in their own range, not only inside the scanner's radius. Best behind a cluster of turrets.
turret_radar_turret_tier2_desc: Reinforces the chosen path. Fire Control Array also strips enemy armor, keeps its mark for a while after enemies leave range, and drains a share of their current HP each second. Spotter Uplink grants even more range and bonus critical damage.
turret_support_turret_desc: Does not attack. Boosts the damage of nearby turrets, making clustered defenses much stronger.
turret_support_turret_path_a_desc: Boosts both damage and attack speed of nearby turrets. A powerful scaling support for offensive builds.
turret_support_turret_path_b_desc: Boosts nearby turrets while slowing enemies inside its aura. A defensive support option that gives your whole setup more time.
turret_support_turret_tier2_desc: The damage aura is greatly reinforced, regardless of evolution path.

wiki_stacking_rule_body: Bonuses to the SAME stat add together first, then that combined total multiplies against everything else. Two +50% damage sources give +100% (x2.0), not x2.25. But a damage bonus and an elite bonus are different buckets, so they multiply.
wiki_stacking_order_body: Damage resolves in this order. Each step multiplies the result of the last.
wiki_step_level_note: Each level multiplies damage, capped at {0} per level.
wiki_step_global_note: All traits and spec cards that raise damage share one bucket.
wiki_step_conditional_note: vs. elites, vs. burning, vs. slowed/frozen — each is its own multiplier.
wiki_slow_rule_heading: Slow bonuses scale the slow, not the speed
wiki_slow_rule_body: A slow-strength bonus increases the slow AMOUNT. It does not halve enemy speed. With +100% slow strength, a 25% slow becomes a 50% slow — the enemy moves at 50% speed, not 25%.
wiki_slow_floor_note: Slow alone can never take an enemy below this. Only Freeze and Shock fully stop movement.
wiki_slow_stacking_body: Slows do NOT add up. If a Frost hit and a Suppression aura both affect an enemy, only the STRONGEST applies. Stacking two weak slows is wasted — raise one instead.
wiki_slow_example_note: Enemy moves at {0} of normal speed.
wiki_burn_intro_body: Every hit that applies burn adds its OWN independent stack, each with its own damage and timer. Total burn damage is the SUM of all active stacks — it is not capped to a single application.
wiki_burn_per_stack_note: Of the hit that applied it, spread over the burn duration. Crits apply stronger burns.
wiki_burn_cap_note: The Ember Stacker and Wildfire evolutions raise this.
wiki_burn_rule_blast_note: A blast applies burn to each enemy it catches individually, not once for the whole blast.
wiki_burn_rule_sources_note: Stacks from different towers and different levels coexist. Nothing is overwritten by source.
wiki_burn_rule_atcap_note: A stronger hit replaces the weakest stack. A weaker hit only refreshes that stack's timer, adding no damage.
wiki_burn_rule_spread_note: Spread burns carry this share of the original damage and duration, and compete for a stack slot like any other application.
wiki_chain_intro_heading: Each hop is weaker than the last
wiki_chain_intro_body: A chain keeps {0} of its damage on every hop, compounding. The falloff is fixed — it does NOT improve with turret level or evolution. Levels raise the starting damage; evolutions and bonuses raise the number of hops.
wiki_chain_table_body: As a share of the primary target's hit.
wiki_chain_inherit_heading: Chain damage uses your damage bonuses
wiki_chain_inherit_body: Chain hits are not a separate flat calculation. They start from the turret's fully-modified damage, and every hop re-checks conditional bonuses and can critically hit on its own.
wiki_chain_bounce_body: Yes — the chain CAN return to the target it started on. Each secondary hop rolls independently, so more hops means more chances to bounce back.
wiki_chain_bounce_damage_note: Of the hop that triggered it — not of the original hit.
wiki_turret_scaling_body: Damage compounds per level. Range grows linearly. These are base values before run bonuses.
wiki_evo_no_stat_change: Keeps the base turret's stats and changes its behaviour instead.
wiki_suppression_body: Both the slow and the radius grow with level. The radius is this turret's own range, so range bonuses widen the field.
wiki_suppression_aura_power_note: Aura Power raises damage and attack-speed auras only. It does not strengthen this slow.
wiki_radar_reveal_body: Reveal range is the Scanner's real stat: it sets the reveal bubble and the radius of both evolutions. Signature bonuses scale it.
wiki_radar_mark_body: Every enemy inside the reveal range is marked, stealth or not. The mark raises the damage they take from every source, and does not stack between multiple Scanners - the strongest mark wins.
wiki_radar_uplink_body: Turrets inside the reveal range can target stealth enemies anywhere in their own range, not only inside the bubble, and gain extra range.
wiki_locked_body: This turret is not available yet. Meet the condition below to add it to your build options.

trait_effect_type_precision_covenant: Railgun Expose, +50% crit damage, -50% chain damage, -20% attack speed

spell_breach_protocol_desc: Exposes every enemy on the map, making them take 35% more damage from all sources for 8 seconds.
spell_aegis_protocol_desc: Restores 3 lives on a long cooldown. Your only answer to a leak.
turret_void_turret_path_a_desc: Weaken hits much harder on a single target.
turret_void_turret_path_b_desc: Weaken spreads a slow to nearby enemies too.
turret_void_turret_tier2_desc: Weaken corrodes armor much further, regardless of evolution path.
turret_toxin_turret_path_a_desc: Fires faster and the toxin's pure damage is much stronger.
turret_toxin_turret_path_b_desc: Deals much higher direct damage per hit.
turret_toxin_turret_tier2_desc: The toxin's pure damage is greatly reinforced, regardless of evolution path.
turret_railgun_turret_path_a_desc: Even higher damage per shot and a longer Expose window, at the cost of fire rate.
turret_railgun_turret_path_b_desc: Fires much more often, trading per-shot power for Expose uptime.
turret_railgun_turret_tier2_desc: Expose amplifies damage taken much further, regardless of evolution path.
wiki_mit_rule_heading: Damage is reduced twice before it lands
wiki_mit_rule_body: Turret-type affinity applies first: an enemy resistant to Frost takes less from every Frost source, and nothing else. Armor applies second and reduces every source equally. The two multiply, so a resistant AND armored enemy is much tougher than either stat alone suggests.
wiki_mit_formula_body: raw damage x (1 - affinity) x (1 - armor) x (1 + expose)
wiki_mit_armor_cap_note: No enemy mitigates more than this, however high the wave.
wiki_mit_resist_cap_note: Applies only to the turret type the enemy resists.
wiki_mit_weak_cap_note: Affinity can go negative. A turret type an enemy is weak to deals up to double.
wiki_mit_min_hit_note: Mitigation can stall a build but never completely wall it.
wiki_mit_pierce_body: Four different effects reduce mitigation, and they compose rather than overwriting each other.
wiki_mit_armor_pierce_note: A flat subtraction that works on every enemy, whatever its type.
wiki_mit_affinity_pierce_note: It cannot deepen a weakness. Against an enemy already weak to that turret type it does nothing.
wiki_mit_weaken_note: A timed status, so it benefits the whole team while it lasts, not only the Void turret.
wiki_mit_shred_note: Applied before the flat pierces, so shred and pierce stack usefully instead of one making the other redundant.
wiki_mit_expose_body: Expose (Railgun) and the Scanner's mark share ONE additive bucket, applied last — after resistance and armor. Because it scales the damage that survived mitigation, it is worth most on targets you are already hurting, and least on ones you cannot dent.
wiki_mit_pure_heading: Pure damage ignores all of it
wiki_mit_pure_body: Toxin's signature damage and health-decay effects bypass affinity, armor and the minimum-damage floor entirely. They gain nothing from Expose either. Against a heavily armored boss, pure damage is the most predictable damage in the game.
wiki_mit_live_plague_note: Share of Toxin's pure damage that your non-Toxin turrets also apply.
wiki_target_rule_heading: Every turret picks one target per shot
wiki_target_rule_body: Which enemy it picks is set by that turret's targeting mode. You can change it per turret from the turret panel, and the choice is saved with your run. Support and Scanner have no mode — they affect everything in radius instead.
wiki_target_first_note: Measured by progress along the path, not spawn order. The default, and the right answer when leaks are what is killing you.
wiki_target_last_note: Softens a wave before it reaches your killzone. Pairs well with slows and burns, which need time to pay off.
wiki_target_strongest_note: Judged on MAXIMUM health, not current, so the turret does not drift off a target as it is worn down. Locks onto elites and bosses.
wiki_target_closest_note: Shortest projectile travel, so the least damage wasted on enemies that die in flight. Best for slow projectiles.
wiki_target_blind_body: A target that cannot be seen is not a target at all — no targeting mode reaches it, and damage bonuses do nothing about it.
wiki_target_stealth_note: Only turrets that can target stealth engage them. A Scanner reveals them for everything nearby, which is what it is for.
wiki_target_flying_note: They fly straight from entry to exit, covering far less ground and spending much less time in range. Cover that straight line, not only the road.
wiki_target_placement_body: Turrets occupy tiles and enemies walk around them, so where you build changes the route — and a longer route means more time inside your ranges. You can never seal the path completely: a placement that would leave no route to the exit is rejected. Lengthening the walk is a real strategy; walling is not an option.
wiki_econ_rule_heading: Upgrade cost compounds faster than damage
wiki_econ_rule_body: Each upgrade costs {0} of the last, while damage grows more slowly. Cost is deliberately priced at roughly the SQUARE of power: doubling a turret's damage costs about four times the gold. Deep upgrades and new turrets are meant to stay competitive with each other — neither is a trap.
wiki_econ_curve_body: As a multiple of the turret's level-1 upgrade cost.
wiki_econ_sell_note: Of the TOTAL gold invested, upgrades included — so relocating a developed turret is not ruinous.
wiki_econ_evolve_note: Choosing a path is free. The second tier is not.
wiki_econ_tier2_note: Priced off the curve above, so evolving a high-level turret is expensive by design.
wiki_econ_kill_gold: Gold per kill grows with the wave
wiki_econ_kill_gold_note: Of the enemy's base reward, per wave reached. Income keeps pace with enemy health.
wiki_econ_skip_note: Preparation is {0}s. Skipping is a genuine income source, not only a way to save time — and it scales with the wave.
wiki_econ_xp_body: Kills award XP as well as gold. Levelling offers spec cards, so clearing waves faster compounds into a stronger build, not just more gold.
wiki_econ_xp_kill: Kill XP grows with the wave
wiki_econ_live_cost_note: Below x1.00 is a discount. Cursed and Greed tiles change this per turret on top of it.
wiki_freeze_body: Freeze is not a very strong slow — it is a hard stop, and it ignores the speed floor that limits slows. Frozen targets also take amplified damage if you have invested in that, which makes a freeze window the moment to land your biggest hits.
wiki_freeze_immunity_note: After a freeze ends, that enemy cannot be refrozen for this long. Without it, a fast turret would freeze-lock a target permanently.
wiki_freeze_locked_out_note: The application is not wasted — it is downgraded, so Frost keeps contributing during the lockout.
wiki_freeze_stacking_note: A freeze is only applied to a target that is not already frozen. More freeze sources means better coverage, not longer freezes.
wiki_shock_heading: Shock — a brief stop, rolled per hit
wiki_shock_body: Shock is the other hard stop. It is far shorter than a freeze but has no immunity window, so it is rolled fresh on every single hit. Its value scales with how often you shoot, not with how hard you hit.
wiki_shock_roll_note: Fast turrets get far more shock uptime than slow ones at the same chance.
wiki_debuff_rule_heading: Two ways to make a target take more
wiki_debuff_rule_body: You can strip what an enemy has, or amplify what you land. Weaken strips armor. Expose amplifies the damage that survived armor. They apply at different points in the damage formula, so running both is not redundant — it is the strongest thing you can do to a single tough target.
wiki_debuff_weaken_body: The Void turret's signature. It subtracts from the target's effective armor for its duration, so every turret shooting that target benefits, not just the Void turret that applied it.
wiki_debuff_weaken_scaling_note: Strength and duration both scale, up to {0}.
wiki_debuff_expose_body: The Railgun's signature. It multiplies ALL mitigated damage the target takes, applied as the very last step — after resistance and armor. It does not affect pure damage, which already bypasses mitigation entirely.
wiki_debuff_mark_heading: The Scanner's mark shares Expose's slot
wiki_debuff_mark_body: Fire Control Array marks every enemy in reveal range, and that mark is ADDED to Expose rather than multiplying with it. A Railgun and a Scanner covering the same corner amplify strongly, not explosively — that is deliberate. Marks from two Scanners do not stack either: the strongest wins.
wiki_debuff_order_body: Armor reduction and damage amplification are different steps. See Damage & Mitigation for the full formula.
wiki_debuff_order_weaken_note: Worth most against heavily armored targets, and nothing at all against unarmored ones.
wiki_debuff_order_expose_note: Worth the same percentage against every target, armored or not.
wiki_debuff_duration_note: Refreshed by every new application — it does not stack up, it stays on.
wiki_debuff_mark_amp_note: Grows per Scanner level. The per-level figure is on the Scanner's own page.
wiki_debuff_mark_shred_note: A proportional cut applied before flat pierce, so the Scanner's Tier 2 does both jobs at once.
wiki_poison_rule_heading: Damage measured in percent, not points
wiki_poison_rule_body: Most damage is a flat number that armor then reduces. These effects take a SHARE of the target's current health instead, so they are worth exactly as much against a wave-100 boss as against a wave-10 grunt. That is what keeps them relevant when enemy health has run away from your turrets.
wiki_poison_toxin_body: Every Toxin hit deals bonus damage equal to a share of the target's CURRENT health, as PURE damage: it ignores armor, ignores resistance, ignores the minimum-damage floor, and gains nothing from Expose. It is the most predictable damage in the game and the answer to an enemy you cannot dent.
wiki_poison_tier2_note: Per hit, on top of the base rate.
wiki_poison_scaling_note: Up to {0}. Attack speed matters more than raw damage here — the effect is per HIT, not per point of damage.
wiki_poison_covenant_body: With the covenant active, turrets that are NOT Toxin also apply a fraction of Toxin's percent damage on their hits, using Toxin's base rate since they have none of their own. A wide board of fast turrets gets far more out of it than a few slow heavy hitters.
wiki_poison_mitigated_heading: Not all percent damage is pure
wiki_poison_mitigated_body: Some evolutions add current-HP damage that is folded into the normal hit and therefore still goes through armor and resistance. It scales the same way but is not immune to mitigation the way Toxin's is — against a heavily armored target the two behave very differently.
wiki_poison_decay_heading: Entropy Engine — decay that cannot kill
wiki_poison_decay_body: Decay removes a share of every enemy's current health each second, everywhere on the board at once, with no turret involved. It is strictly non-lethal: it stops at a floor and your turrets still have to finish the job. Treat it as softening, never as a win condition.
wiki_poison_decay_floor_note: Of maximum health. Decay never takes an enemy below this, and never lands the killing blow.
wiki_poison_decay_numbers_note: Decay ticks every frame on every enemy, so it is silent by design. It still counts toward percent-HP damage totals.
wiki_waves_rule_heading: Enemy health accelerates — your damage does not
wiki_waves_rule_body: Health does not grow at a fixed rate. The rate itself climbs, from gentle early growth to a much steeper late curve, so every run is designed to end. The question is never whether the curve catches you, only how far you get first.
wiki_waves_growth_body: How much each wave multiplies enemy health, at that point in the run.
wiki_waves_growth_cap_note: The rate stops climbing here. It never stops compounding.
wiki_waves_speed_none: Enemies do not get faster as the waves go on — only tougher and more numerous. A slow bought at wave 10 is worth exactly as much at wave 100.
wiki_waves_speed_some: Most enemies do not speed up at all as the waves go on. A few — bosses mainly — gain up to {0} per wave, which is nothing next to how fast health climbs. Slows keep their value for the whole run.
wiki_waves_size_body: Each wave spends a budget on enemies. The budget grows both linearly and quadratically, so later waves are not just tougher one at a time — there are far more of them, arriving faster.
wiki_waves_spawn_interval_note: Shrinks by {0} each wave, down to a floor of {1}.
wiki_waves_tiers_body: Elite and boss waves are on fixed schedules, so they are the one part of the run you can prepare for exactly. A boss wave never also spawns elites.
wiki_waves_boss_note: The boss always spawns last in its wave.
wiki_waves_tier_hp_note: On top of the wave scaling above. Gold rewards use the same multipliers.
wiki_enemies_rule_body: Most enemies just walk the path and die. The types below each invalidate something a defence normally relies on — the route, your line of sight, or the idea that damage dealt stays dealt. A build that handles all of them is what carries a run past the first boss.
wiki_enemy_tank_note: The armor is the real problem, not the health. Pierce or pure damage, not more raw damage.
wiki_enemy_sprinter_note: Dies instantly if it is hit at all. The danger is that it crosses your range before anything fires.
wiki_enemy_stealth_note: Ignored entirely by turrets that cannot see stealth, however strong they are. A Scanner solves it for everything nearby.
wiki_enemy_flying_note: Flies straight from entry to exit, so it spends far less time in range. Fragile to compensate.
wiki_enemy_berserk_val: speeds up to {0} as it is hurt
wiki_enemy_berserk_val_plain: speeds up as it is hurt
wiki_enemy_berserk_note: Chipping it is the worst outcome. Either kill it outright or keep it slowed.
wiki_enemy_splitter_note: Kill it early on the path, not at your base — the children still have the whole route left to walk.
wiki_enemy_regen_val: heals {0} of max health per second
wiki_enemy_regen_note: Beats slow chip damage outright. Burst it down, or out-tick it with burn and poison.
wiki_enemy_buffer_note: Kill it first and the whole wave gets easier. Target it before the crowd it is buffing.
wiki_enemy_debuffer_note: Only affects turrets inside its radius, so it punishes tightly packed defences hardest.
wiki_enemies_tiers_heading: Tiers stack on top of type
wiki_enemies_tiers_body: Elite and boss are not separate enemies — they are the same types with a health multiplier. An elite Regenerator still regenerates, and now has five times the health to regenerate. Some enemies only ever appear as elites or bosses and never in a normal wave.
wiki_cards_rule_heading: Bad luck is compensated, not just survived
wiki_cards_rule_body: Card rarity is weighted, but the weights are not fixed. Every offer that misses a rarity raises your odds for the next one, and past a certain number of misses the game simply gives it to you. A drought is temporary by design.
wiki_cards_unavailable_body: The card settings could not be read, so the exact numbers are not shown here.
wiki_cards_weights_body: Before any pity. These are relative weights across the cards you can still be offered.
wiki_cards_pity_body: Each rarity has its own counter. Odds start improving at the first number and the rarity is guaranteed at the second.
wiki_cards_duplicates_note: You will never be shown the same card twice in a single offer.
wiki_cards_early_heading: The best cards are gated by wave
wiki_cards_early_body: High rarities are held back early so a lucky first level-up cannot decide the whole run. Their odds are suppressed before their minimum wave, and the pity counters keep running in the meantime — so they can land quickly once the gate opens.
wiki_tiles_rule_body: Some tiles change whatever is built on them. A tile's effect is a separate multiplier from your global bonuses, so it multiplies against everything else rather than being diluted by it — which is why matching the right turret to the right tile is worth going out of your way for.
wiki_tiles_share_note: Rolled when the map is generated, so a board's special tiles are fixed for the whole run.
wiki_tiles_blessed_body: A straight bonus with no cost. Put your strongest turret on one.
wiki_tiles_cursed_heading: Curses — a penalty you are paid for
wiki_tiles_cursed_body: Most curses cripple one stat and compensate with another, and those are not traps: a turret that does not care about the penalty gets the compensation for free — a range penalty costs a short-range turret almost nothing. A few curses are pure downside, with nothing listed after the slash. Build on those only when you have run out of better ground.
wiki_tiles_greed_body: Greed tiles trade upgrade cost for power in one direction or the other. Whether they are good depends entirely on how much gold you expect to sink into that turret for the rest of the run.
